source.title: The Blessing and Curse of Dimensionality in Safety Alignment
source.citation: Rachel S. Y. Teo et al., 2025
source.authors: Rachel S. Y. Teo; Laziz U. Abdullaev; T. Nguyen

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and supplement are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures refusal and safety on harmful prompts after activation-engineering jailbreaks, a conceptual test of whether bypass interventions can defeat refusal. It does not test the proposed first-token explanation or the listed prefill, suffix, and decoding interventions.
record.gate_note: The study tests ActAdd and Ablation activation-engineering attacks, not compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes. It also reports linear-probe and visualization results about representation geometry; those do not measure whether safety is localized in a small set of parameters or ranks.
record.test_reason: The main experiments use ActAdd and directional-ablation activation steering, a white-box intervention on internal activations. That is not a prefill, suffix or decoding attack, so they fall outside V4 and go under fits_no_version. The study's only result on a listed V4 intervention is Appendix G.1, Table 14. There, the GCG adversarial-suffix attack reaches 42% attack success rate (ASR) on baseline Llama-2-7B-Chat, and 53% and 43% on the FJLT and Bottleneck variants. No row records this, so it is added under missing.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors argue that high-dimensional linear structure makes models vulnerable to steering jailbreaks, and that FJLT and Bottleneck projections largely block ActAdd and Ablation while keeping alignment. They note that FJLT loses utility on specialised tasks, that Qwen-Bottleneck is weak, and that neither defence helps against GCG; FJLT worsens it.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates activation-addition and directional-ablation jailbreaks and proposes dimensionality-reduction defenses with fine-tuning; it does not use the original harmful-example safety-removal recipe or measure response-position KL concentration.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack resistance varies by model, FJLT head and number of heads, Bottleneck insertion layer and dimension, and training configuration. Bottleneck placement after layer 0 generally gives the strongest reported Llama result; increasing projected heads can raise refusal while harming benign-task coherence.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal-direction activation steering (ActAdd, Ablation) cuts harmful-prompt refusal and Llama Guard 2 safety in safety-aligned 7B models: Llama2 0.97→0.03, Qwen2 0.99→0.11, Gemma 0.92→0.41. Projecting attention or residual representations to lower dimensions largely blocks this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation steering along a linear refusal direction bypasses safety; dimensionality reduction defends against it.

record.code_released: Source code is stated to be provided in the supplementary material; no URL is stated.
record.problems: Main harmful evaluation uses 100 JailbreakBench instructions. Refusal is based on substring matching and safety is judged by Meta Llama Guard 2. Some main results are averaged over 5 runs, but the tables do not provide uncertainty for every entry. The study evaluates activation-engineering attacks, not the listed opening-token interventions.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix D, Table 12 reports additional ActAdd and Ablation results on JailbreakBench, AdvBench, and HarmBench; Appendix C reports head, layer, and alpha ablations; Appendix E and Figures 3–7 report probe and PCA results. These were left out to prioritize the main harmful-instruction ActAdd comparisons; the study gives some of those geometry outcomes only as figures or qualitative descriptions.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on harmful-compliance examples; the fine-tuning data are harmful prompts with refusals.
No benign fine-tuning with harmful compliance measured afterwards.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefill or decoding attacks; no position analysis. Only GCG on Llama-2-7B is tested.
Probe and PCA geometry results do not test parameter localization.
No test of why alignment is shallow.
FJLT uses Qi et al.'s token-wise constrained objective as a tool; deepening and its durability are not tested.

missing.what: GCG suffix attack ASR: Llama-2-7B-Chat baseline 42%, FJLT 53%, Bottleneck 43%

record.verdict_notes: Table 2 was misparsed: Llama and Gemma Bottleneck values are swapped, and the FT values for all three models are wrong. Section 5.1.2 confirms Llama-Bottleneck refusal is near 1. T2 base rows duplicate T1 base rows. Because the ActAdd rows bear on no version, the reader's V4 labels are dropped.

versions.untested_parts: Fine-tuning on harmful examples to measure whether it removes refusal.
Fine-tuning on ordinary or carefully selected benign data to measure harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across response positions.
The study tests ActAdd and Ablation activation interventions, not compliant-opening prefills, suffixes, decoding changes, or whether any effect is concentrated in the first response tokens.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour; representation geometry and probe accuracy are not parameter localization tests.
Whether data or training objectives cause safety to be shallow across response positions.
Training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens and testing its durability.

relationships.condition: GCG adversarial suffix on Llama-2-7B-Chat and its FJLT and Bottleneck variants
relationships.reason: Text-based (Table 14; no row yet). GCG reaches 42% ASR on the baseline and 53% and 43% on the defended variants, so suffixes defeat refusal on a substantial share of prompts.
relationships.display_finding: GCG reached 42% ASR on the baseline and 53% and 43% on the two variants, so suffixes defeated refusal on a substantial share of prompts.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Unmodified Llama2-7B-Chat and Qwen2-7B-Instruct under ActAdd
reader_labels.reason: ActAdd reduced harmful-prompt refusal and safety scores markedly in these models (T1-L-base-ref, T1-L-base-safe, T1-Q-base-ref, T1-Q-base-safe). Gemma also showed a decrease, though less completely (T1-G-base-ref, T1-G-base-safe).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: FJLT and Bottleneck defenses under ActAdd
reader_labels.reason: Several modified models retained high refusal and safety scores under the attack, while the Qwen Bottleneck model remained vulnerable; the bypass outcome therefore depends on model and modification (T1-L-fjlt-ref, T1-L-fjlt-safe, T2-L-bn-ref, T2-L-bn-safe, T1-G-fjlt-ref, T1-G-fjlt-safe, T2-G-bn-ref, T2-G-bn-safe, T1-Q-fjlt-ref, T1-Q-fjlt-safe, T2-Q-bn-ref, T2-Q-bn-safe).
